records.subagent_summary: All 8 rollouts scored 0 (execution 149.278): seven boxed 143, one 154, none hit the token cap. Every rollout opened the two readings of the public number as separate self-contained cases, argued inside each that a speaker's own value plus that reading pins the partner, wrote "contradiction", then abandoned logic and picked a factor on looks (one explicitly chose the value it wrongly called non-unique among factor pairs). Not one built a single joint object over value and reading, and not one used the first speaker's ignorance as a filter on the second speaker's candidate partners. The prose incumbent already says all this abstractly and still fails, so the revision replaces prose with one concrete artifact - a value-by-choice table with blank-on-illegal cells, filled-cell counting per row, and ignorance propagation as blanking cells whose partner row is not ignorant - giving a mechanical procedure instead of a principle.

All 8 rollouts correct (3.0k-9.8k tokens, 4-30 hedges), so training is saturated and the cost is transfer plus waste. Diagnosis: the incumbent's bare 'skip roots of unity' was disobeyed by 7 of 8, which enumerated the n solutions via exponentials (14-129 occurrences) after already having the circle, because they doubted a necessary condition suffices. The worst (9.8k tokens, 30 hedges) derived a bogus side-condition from that enumeration, concluded only 2 of 6 roots fit, and spent ~5k tokens escaping a self-inflicted contradiction; another closed by asserting the modulus condition is 'sufficient', right answer via wrong logic that will not transfer. Also 6 of 8 ignored the prescribed w*wbar clearing and used x+iy anyway. So the revision states WHY necessity closes the problem (containment is what is asked), makes it an explicit stop rule capped at a one-root check, and permits either clearing route.

My 8 rollouts scored 6/8, all finish_reason=stop, so no budget loss: both failures commit a wrong answer via the same containment error. One had the covering square as x,y in [0,2] and S spanning -0.5..0.5, then asserted S was entirely inside even though S reaches negative x and y; it had the right corner frame and never sign-tested one vertex. The other compared a reach radius (~0.707 to S's farthest corner) against the big square's half-diagonal (~1.414) and concluded containment. Neither clipped any region; both answered summed-areas-minus-area(S). The incumbent only asserts overlap lies strictly between 0 and area(S), and a bare bound loses to a concrete-looking radius number. This revision makes the bound executable: list S's vertices in the corner frame, covered iff both coordinates are non-negative, which exposes uncovered vertices directly, and defines overlap as S clipped to the quadrant so a computation follows.

5/8 correct. All three failures came from misreading T. One quoted the hint's cap verbatim, then assumed T was itself a fifth-degree polynomial value, so 'degree-1 T cannot cancel P's leading term' carried no force; it dropped the per-group cap and drifted to N=10. One computed N x d correctly, called it 'too high', and reverted to a small guess before truncating. The third never grouped at all: it chained adjacent board entries, built the P+d shift family, and reported N=10. So the live fault is that T is not recognised as the progression's own affine formula, and that position index versus substituted argument look like two variables. The revision states T's degree explicitly, folds the consecutive-input shift into one variable so P keeps degree d, and keeps the per-group cap, the N x d aggregation, and the block construction.

6/8 correct (jobs 149.282). Both failures hit the token cap on the same jam, not on the reduction: they fit the curve, formed the closure f(t+dx)=f(t)+dy, and got the right quadratic with jointly the degenerate root and the wanted one. They then read the non-degenerate vertex's height off the log with the exponent's sign flipped (an argument well under 1 was assigned a negative height), so the translated vertex missed the curve. Both jointly declared a contradiction: one looped re-expanding identical algebra, the other pivoted to the banned equal-diagonal-midpoints condition, collapsed the figure onto a given vertex, then produced a negative discriminant and 11 'no real solution' jams. The incumbent already says 'take each height from f', so the missing mechanism is a cheap verification of that single log evaluation: exponentiate the height back and compare it to the argument, and treat a curve miss as one wrong exponent sign to repair rather than a broken problem.

3/8 correct (idx 0,2,7) and even those got 1/8 unsoundly: idx 7 pattern-matched 1/2^(n-1), idx 0 and 2 inverted the pile (bottom = last carried) yet luckily still multiplied three halves. Failures: idx 3,6 called the shed a uniform random permutation (1/24, then 1/4); idx 5 declared the order always reversed (1, 0); idx 1 paired a right part a with a non-probabilistic 1/3; idx 4 hit the token cap oscillating over which end of the shed is the bottom. So the incumbent states the orientation rule and bans 1/n, yet the flip survives in 6 of 8 and prose narration of moves burns tokens. This revision keeps arrival-rank orientation and forced/free 1/2 pricing, adding two mechanisms: first hand-check the model on the two-item instance, which concretely refutes forced-order and uniformity and pins orientation, and record moves as a compact in/out letter string instead of prose. Measured 190 tokens.

4/8. All four winners did only this: solve n=2,3,4 numerically, fit a signed reciprocal-factorial law, substitute. Three of the four failures hit the 16384 cap the same way: after spending 1000+ tokens re-arguing how many conditions a size-n toy carries, each abandoned numbers for symbolic general-size algebra (coefficient of x in a product of linear factors, elementary symmetric sums, harmonic sums); when that formula clashed with a toy they had computed correctly, all three kept re-deriving the symbolic formula instead of trusting the number. The fourth built no toy at all, named 'moment theory', and asserted a wrong sign and factorial argument. So this revision bans carrying the stated size as a symbol, replaces formula-guessing with consecutive ratios (growth and sign come out mechanically), makes computed cases authoritative over any law, and routes ambiguity to one extra numeric case.

All 8 public rollouts scored reward 1 (train 8/8), so headroom is transfer only (incumbent 14/80). But runs were expensive and unstable: 5.6k-11.2k completion tokens with 10-41 'wait' backtracks, and every rollout kept resurrecting the group-count reading (3-21 mentions of the rival price it implies) before returning to the gcd count. The churn is not arithmetic; it is re-litigating whether each listed figure is a village grand total or a per-house amount. The incumbent only says 'decide once', giving no test, so rollouts oscillate. Prior rounds show deleting the gcd/max-count mechanic collapses train (8/8 to 3/8) and a maximality certificate hurt heldout (5/80), so I kept round 13's structure and swapped the vague 'decide once' clause for a portable well-posedness test: prefer the reading under which every stated condition does work and the hidden count is determined. That should terminate the same oscillation on unseen items of this class.

7 of 8 rollouts correct (3.4k-4.8k tokens). The single failure burned the full 16384-token cap from one algebra slip: it read the incumbent's AB(A^(n-1)-B^(n-1))=0 and rewrote AB^3-BA^3 as AB^2(B-A), so the only surviving branch was B=A. That contradicts distinct p(0),q(0), so it concluded no common fixed point exists (38 'fixed point', 9 'another', 11 'A = B', 5 'contradiction' mentions), abandoned the centered ansatz, and never recovered. The 7 correct rollouts all wrote B=-A within their first page and finished quickly, so the branch enumeration is the whole gap. This revision keeps the proven trigger, ansatz, parameter-count closure, symmetric-combination and verification spine and changes only the branch step into a portable root-enumeration rule, plus a switch-roots-not-ansatz recovery instruction.

4/8 correct. All four failures share one move: they never traced a state, they wrote cycle notation inferred from the sub-steps' shapes. Two announced the composite was disjoint transpositions/short cycles and reported an off-by-one exponent; one invented per-size cycle lists (2,4,2 then 2,8,2,4) that no trace produced; one fabricated counts for the two smallest sizes, got contradictory numbers, and fit an inflated exponent. One failure explicitly noticed its formula contradicted the smallest size and excused it as a special case; another oscillated between order 2 and a growing order and burned the whole budget. Correct rollouts instead traced slot movement and reported one consistent growth law. So the revision bans deriving cycle type from sub-step shapes, demands each count come from a written state trace, and forces the fitted formula to be re-checked against the smallest size with no exceptions allowed.
